clue.text: Do they give assistance to the " Frothblowers '?

definitions.text: Do they give assistance to the " Frothblowers '?

parts.words: Do they give assistance to the " Frothblowers '?
parts.note: froth blowers are beer drinkers who blow the head off a pint; those who help them are the women serving behind a pub counter

explanation.walkthrough: The Ancient Order of Froth Blowers was a British drinking fraternity of the 1920s; 'Frothblowers' here means any beer drinkers.
explanation.definitionFit: Women who pull pints in a pub serve the drinkers who blow away the froth.

clue.text: But it's not everything in a girl's make-up !

definitions.text: But it's not everything in a girl's make-up !

parts.words: But it's not everything in a girl's make-up !
parts.note: the nursery rhyme says girls are made of sugar and spice and all things nice; the spice is only part of the recipe

explanation.walkthrough: The rhyme 'What are little girls made of?' answers 'sugar and spice and all things nice'; the clue reads the answer as 'all spice', which is not everything.
explanation.definitionFit: A spice from the dried berry of a tropical tree, read here as 'all of the spice'.

clue.text: False declaration by a spinster, we hear ?

definitions.text: False declaration by a spinster, we hear ?

parts.words: False declaration by a spinster, we hear ?
parts.note: an untrue claim, which said out loud sounds like a statement made by an unmarried woman, a Miss

explanation.walkthrough: A spinster is addressed as Miss, so a declaration by her would be a 'Miss statement', which sounds just like the word for an inaccurate claim.
explanation.definitionFit: An untrue or inaccurate claim, sounding like a declaration from a Miss.

clue.text: Preparation for drawing in

definitions.text: Preparation for drawing in

parts.note: preparation suggests getting ready to sketch, but it is a medicinal preparation that is breathed in

explanation.walkthrough: 'Preparation for drawing' reads as setting up an easel; the drawing in is drawing breath, and the preparation is a medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: A medicine taken by breathing it into the lungs.

clue.text: The backing of horses ?

definitions.text: The backing of horses ?

parts.note: backing horses suggests betting on them, but here it is what sits on a horse's back

explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' looks like gambling; it means the gear placed on the horse's back.
explanation.definitionFit: Riders' seats strapped onto the backs of horses.

clue.text: Ingots liquefied ?

definitions.text: Ingots liquefied ?

indicators.note: melting gold bars would let them flow into new shapes, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does both jobs: 'liquefied' rearranges INGOTS, and the result is a liquid, an old name for strong ale.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for strong ale or beer, a drink made from the bars' letters.

clue.text: Victor gets an embrace and nothing more

definitions.text: Victor

parts.note: a hug is an embrace
O looks like the figure zero

explanation.surface: A winner receives a hug and nothing else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Victor' looks like a winner, but it is the first name of the French novelist who wrote Les Misérables; 'and' and 'more' only join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The author of Les Misérables was Victor, so his surname completes the name.

clue.text: Man's law is administered by him

definitions.text: Man's law is administered by him

parts.words: Man's law is administered by him
parts.note: mankind's law seems meant, but Man is the Isle of Man, whose judges have their own title

explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is the Isle of Man, a self-governing island in the Irish Sea; its two senior judges are called deemsters.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of a judge on the Isle of Man, who deems or judges cases there.

clue.text: Something gained by an uprising

definitions.text: Something gained by an uprising

parts.note: an uprising suggests a rebellion winning territory, but read literally it is a climb, which gains height

explanation.walkthrough: 'Uprising' looks political, but it means going up, and what is gained by going up is height above the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Height above sea level is what an aircraft or climber gains by going up.

clue.text: They are the subject of drawings by 1

definitions.text: They are the subject of drawings by 1

parts.words: They are the subject of drawings by 1
parts.note: drawings suggest pictures, but the women at 1 across draw beers from the pump

explanation.walkthrough: '1' points to 1 across, the women behind a pub counter; to draw beer is to pull it from the cask, so their drawings are pints of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Barmaids draw beers, so beers are what their drawings are of.

clue.text: Where drinks if not seats are freely given ?

definitions.text: Where drinks if not seats are freely given ?

parts.words: Where drinks if not seats are freely given ?
parts.note: to stand someone a drink is to buy it for them, so a place where drinks are stood but there are no seats

explanation.walkthrough: To 'stand' a drink is British for paying for it; a crowded pub with no seats is space where people stand, and where drinks are stood.
explanation.definitionFit: Space with no seats where people must remain upright, as in a packed bar.

clue.text: Seat for a Professor of Petrology ?

definitions.text: Seat for a Professor of Petrology ?

parts.words: Seat for a Professor of Petrology ?
parts.note: a professor holds a chair, and petrology is the study of rocks, so a chair in rocks

explanation.walkthrough: A professorship is called a chair; a chair in the study of rocks becomes a chair that sways back and forth.
explanation.definitionFit: A seat on curved runners that sways to and fro, read as a professorship in rocks.

clue.text: Old-time Channel Islands bus conductor, a chirpy creature

definitions.text: a chirpy creature

parts.note: in Victorian London a cad was the conductor on a horse-drawn omnibus

explanation.surface: A sketch of an old Channel Islands bus conductor who is cheerful company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old-time' at the front tells you the bus conductor is an old one: CAD was the Victorian name for the man who took fares on a horse-drawn omnibus.
explanation.definitionFit: This insect is known for the loud chirping song the males make in summer.

clue.text: The last person to help keep up one's spirits

definitions.text: The last person to help keep up one's spirits

parts.words: The last person to help keep up one's spirits
parts.note: keeping up spirits means cheering someone, but here the spirits are ghosts, which this person drives out rather than keeps

explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirits' reads as morale; it means ghosts or demons, and the person who casts them out is the last one to keep them around.
explanation.definitionFit: A priest who casts out demons and ghosts is the opposite of someone who keeps them.

clue.text: This letter only comes in August

definitions.text: This letter only comes in August

parts.words: This letter only comes in August
parts.note: the letter meant is G, number seven in the alphabet, which appears in no other month's name

explanation.walkthrough: Seeming to be about post arriving in summer, the clue means the alphabet's G, its letter number seven: of the twelve month names, only AUGUST contains a G.
explanation.definitionFit: G is the alphabet's letter at position seven, so it is the letter so numbered.

clue.text: Making preparation for business at the hosier's

definitions.text: Making preparation for business at the hosier's

parts.words: Making preparation for business at the hosier's
parts.note: making preparation for business is laying in goods; a hosier sells legwear, one item of which shares the word

explanation.walkthrough: To stock up is to prepare a shop for trade; at the hosier's, a seller of socks and hose, the same word names a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: Filling shelves with goods, and also a garment for the leg sold by a hosier.

clue.text: Marines re-assembled in class

definitions.text: class

indicators.note: the soldiers are put back together in a new formation, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.definitionFit: A small university class meeting for discussion is a tutorial group of this kind.

clue.text: With which to see 22 beheaded possibly

definitions.text: With which to see 22 beheaded possibly

indicators.note: the letters could possibly be arranged otherwise, so they are rearranged
the head is cut off, so the first letter goes

parts.note: 22 across is a number four twenties

explanation.surface: A grim instruction to watch someone being beheaded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beheaded' drops the E from EIGHTY (22 across) to leave IGHTY; with SEE, 'possibly' rearranges the lot, and the whole clue defines the answer as what one sees with.
explanation.definitionFit: The faculty of sight, which is what anyone uses to see.

clue.text: They're not made nowadays

definitions.text: They're not made nowadays

parts.note: objects that cannot be made today because their value lies in having been made long ago

explanation.walkthrough: The complaint 'they don't make them like that any more' is true by definition of old collectable pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Collectable old objects valued because they come from a past age.

clue.text: Gains for which an ex-amateur is well suited

definitions.text: Gains

parts.note: an amateur who turns professional is a pro
something that fits is well suited

explanation.surface: Earnings that an athlete newly turned professional is right for.
explanation.definitionFit: Financial returns or earnings after costs are what a business gains.

clue.text: In short in a royal corps he'd be nothing without 17

definitions.text: In short in a royal corps he'd be nothing without 17

parts.words: In short in a royal corps he'd be nothing without 17
parts.note: the Royal ... Corps is shortened to ROC, in which this man is the O; and a watcher is nothing without sight

explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Observer Corps was a British civil defence body that watched for aircraft; its short form is ROC, and the man who watches stands for the O, 'nothing'. 17 is eyesight, which he could not work without.
explanation.definitionFit: A man whose job is to watch the skies depends on being able to see.

clue.text: Watchman entertained at home.

definitions.text: Watchman entertained at home.

parts.note: a watchman seems a guard, but here he is someone entertained at home by watching television

explanation.walkthrough: 'Watchman' suggests a night guard; it is anyone who watches, and the one entertained at home is a television audience member.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who watches television, entertained without leaving the house.

clue.text: Score less than a century

definitions.text: Score less than a century

parts.note: in cricket a score short of a hundred; but a score is also twenty, and four of them fall short of a hundred

explanation.walkthrough: The cricket reading (a batsman out before reaching 100) misleads; four score is a number twenty short of a century of one hundred.
explanation.definitionFit: Four twenties make a number below one hundred, so the clue describes the number four score.

clue.text: Pretty awkward mess — there's a catch in it

definitions.text: Pretty awkward mess — there's a catch in it

parts.words: Pretty awkward mess — there's a catch in it
parts.note: a pretty awkward mess is an idiom for a muddle, and a pan holding a catch from the river is the same phrase taken literally

explanation.walkthrough: 'A pretty kettle of fish' is an old British idiom for an awkward situation; read literally it is a pot with a catch of fish inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a troublesome muddle, also literally a cooking pot full of a day's catch.

clue.text: Her attachment to Poe makes her also write verse

definitions.text: Her attachment to Poe makes her also write verse

parts.words: Her attachment to Poe makes her also write verse
parts.note: a girl's name placed after the surname of the American poet Edgar Allan Poe forms a word for a woman who writes poems

explanation.walkthrough: Attaching the girl's name to POE spells POETESS, a woman who writes verse, so she becomes one too.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, best known from Hardy's novel about the D'Urbervilles.

clue.text: Have a drink with Lily in the garden.

definitions.text: Lily in the garden

parts.note: rum is a spirit made from sugar cane

explanation.surface: An invitation to have a drink with a woman called Lily out in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lily' looks like a guest's name; it is the plant, and 'Have' and 'with' only join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The arum is a garden plant whose white flower is called an arum lily.

clue.text: Not knowing of a cosy home outside Nice perhaps

definitions.text: Not knowing

indicators.note: the home is put around the outside of the other letters

parts.note: a nest is a snug home, as in a love nest

indicators.note: the place name might perhaps be spelt another way, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone unaware of a snug home somewhere near Nice on the Riviera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges NICE to CIEN, and 'outside' puts NEST around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal word meaning ignorant, from Latin for lacking knowledge.

clue.text: Swift, for one, starts get getting' changed about one

definitions.text: Swift, for one

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the other piece
the word starts is being altered, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the printed word is a slip for straits, a narrow sea channel, whose seven letters are the ones the anagram needs
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A swift bird, for example, beginning to change direction around someone.
explanation.walkthrough: As printed, 'starts' has six letters and no I, so with 'one' only seven letters result; the fodder that works is STRAITS, rearranged by 'getting changed' around I ('about').
explanation.definitionFit: Jonathan Swift, author of Gulliver's Travels, is the classic example of a writer who mocks society.
